_comment: Tier-2: RingElement3D3N's Check verifies only Id, current length and node count — NOT CROSS_AREA / YOUNG_MODULUS / DENSITY, which it later reads, so a missing CROSS_AREA or YOUNG_MODULUS gives k_0 = 0 and a Newton solve that fails with no actionable error. Pitfall (kratos.cable_net #7, edge 1 of two). Executed on Kratos 10.4.3 (pip wheels, glibc-2.31 host, fresh venv on external ext4 image). MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, not just the permissiveness: a RingElement3D3N built on a Properties object with NOTHING set initialises without complaint and its CalculateLeftHandSide returns a stiffness matrix whose largest absolute entry is EXACTLY 0.0. The same element with YOUNG_MODULUS, DENSITY and CROSS_AREA set returns a non-zero matrix. So the element is not merely indifferent to the missing properties — it silently drops out of the global system, which is the claim's 'silent zero stiffness'. Edge 2 (every translational DOF receiving the full ring mass) is named in the report as not yet done. The fixture imports KratosMultiphysics at module scope; with Kratos absent the import raises, the process exits non-zero and the runner records a failure, never a pass. MUTATION CONTROL (added 2026-08-06, re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 gives the supposedly empty Properties the full CROSS_AREA / YOUNG_MODULUS / DENSITY set, removing the missing-properties condition that produces the silent zero stiffness; the stiffness is then nonzero in both runs. Verified: unmutated the fixture PASSES; with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS and these expect_in_output strings disappear: empty_properties_stiffness_is_exactly_zero=True, ring_check_mismatches=0. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/kratos/cablenet_ring_check_ignores_properties && /usr/bin/python3 source.py (passes), then T2_MUTATE=1 /usr/bin/python3 source.py (fails). Interpreter: KRATOS_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3 is REQUIRED on this host -- the repo venv Kratos wheel is built against GLIBC_2.32 and fails to load (ImportError on Kratos.cpython-312...so), while the system python3.8 carries Kratos 10.4 Release with CableNet, ConstitutiveLaws, StructuralMechanics and LinearSolvers.
